name: Elizur
overview: Elizur was a male leader from the tribe of Reuben during the time of the Exodus. He served as the head of the tribe of Reuben at the time of the census recorded in Numbers 1:5. His leadership role highlights his importance among the Israelites during their wilderness journey.
namesAndTitles: The name Elizur means 'G-d is my Rock,' reflecting a strong declaration of faith in God's steadfastness. This proper name, as given in Numbers 1:5, emphasizes reliance on God as a foundation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Elizur was the father of Shedeur, as explicitly noted in Numbers 1:5. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elizur's significance lies in his role as a tribal leader appointed during the census, a key organizational moment for the Israelites in the wilderness. As head of Reuben, he was responsible for representing his tribe in the larger community of Israel during the Exodus. His leadership under God's guidance reflects the order and structure God established among His people during their journey.
